Practical 12: CI/CD Pipeline with GitHub Actions
Student Name: Krish Bhingradiya
Student ID: 24IT004
GitHub Repository: https://github.com/krishbhingradiya/API-Testing.git
Tech Stack: Node.js & Express
Problem Statement :
  • Set up a GitHub Actions workflow for the Task Management application that runs automatically on every push to the main branch.
  • The pipeline must install dependencies (npm install) as a defined step.
  • The pipeline must run at least one automated test and report a clear pass/fail status.
  • Demonstrate a failed pipeline caused by a deliberately broken test.
  • Demonstrate a fixed pipeline that passes after the test is corrected.
Screenshots & Terminal Execution
Step – 1 : GitHub Actions Workflow Code

The GitHub Actions workflow file is configured in .github/workflows/ci.yml. It listens for push events on the main branch, checks out source code, sets up Node.js 20 LTS, installs packages, and executes the Jest test suite.

Step – 2 : Automated Test code

Automated API tests are implemented in tests/tasks.test.js using Jest and Supertest. In-memory caching and Mongoose query mocks are applied to test real Express endpoints without external database latency.

Step – 5 : Fixed Pipeline & Verification

After observing the deliberate failure, the test expectation was restored to HTTP 200 and committed. GitHub Actions triggered Run #3 and completed with a Green Checkmark.

Conclusion & Learning Outcomes
  • Configured and automated a professional Continuous Integration (CI) pipeline using GitHub Actions for an Express/Node.js REST API.
  • Implemented unit and integration testing with Jest and Supertest, validating status codes, response payloads, and HATEOAS hyperlinks.
  • Verified pipeline resilience through deliberate failure injection (Red X) and subsequent error restoration (Green Checkmark).
  • Embedded an active GitHub Actions workflow status badge into repository documentation to provide immediate pipeline health visibility.
